title: Pages: the first deploy carrying the cave (edc5a2a6, 1,090 files) hung on GitHub's side and every push after it was refused as 'in progress deployment'; cancelled through the Pages API, the next fresh run published; a rerun of a failed publish uploads a second artifact and fails on that
context: After 2026-10-16-descent-mission-first-version the site carries below/ (the cave, 83 files, 9 MB; the artifact 26 MB packed). edc5a2a6's Publish run timed out in actions/deploy-pages at its 10-minute default ('Timeout reached, aborting!') while GitHub kept the deployment 'in progress'; 7f9c1f56's was cancelled by the next push, 055dfaf3's, 9073be5f's and de89b78f's failed with 'Deployment request failed ... due to in progress deployment. Please cancel edc5a2a6 first'. A `gh run rerun --failed` of 9073be5f's publish failed on 'Multiple artifacts named github-pages were unexpectedly found' (the rerun uploads again under the same run). The action clamps `timeout` to 600000 ms (a 30-minute value is set back to it with a warning).
outcome: `gh api -X POST repos/kai-denrei/stalheart/pages/deployments/<sha>/cancel` cancelled the hung deployment; the next push (c47270f9, a fresh run: one artifact) published, the live release.json reads main@c47270f9 and below/index.html answers 200. The workflow's deploy step names the maximum timeout with the note. Lesson: a hung Pages deployment blocks every later one until cancelled; never `rerun --failed` a publish, push a fresh commit instead.
alternatives: Wait for GitHub to time the deployment out on its own: unknown length; the cancel endpoint is immediate.
evidence: gh run list --branch main (edc5a2a6 through c47270f9), gh run view <id> --log-failed; curl https://kai-denrei.github.io/stalheart/release.json, .../below/index.html
